target.title: fix(gateway): re-check session runtime model against current agent defaults after hot-reload
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent model hot-reload (`agents.<id>.model.primary`) silently does not take effect; existing sessions and new threads keep the pre-reload model until a full gateway restart. Re-check persisted session runtime model metadata against current agent defaults so config changes propagate without a restart.

- Problem: After a config hot-reload changes `agents.<id>.model.primary`, the session entry's `modelProvider`/`model` fields (cached from the last reset) are returned by `resolveSessionModelRef` without consulting the current agent config, so new turns and `/new` child sessions inherit the stale model.
- Solution: In the shared `resolveSessionModelRef` resolver, when `modelProvider`/`model` are present and `agentId` is known, verify they still match current agent defaults. If they differ, the config was hot-reloaded — re-resolve from the current config so the session picks up the new model without a restart.
- What changed: `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` (staleness check in `resolveSessionModelRef`), `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` (3 new test cases)
- What did NOT change: Explicit user model overrides (`modelOverride`/`providerOverride`); hot-reload handler; session persistence; `/new` inheritance logic (but it now inherits correctly because the parent's resolution is already fresh)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #102269
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The gateway logs `config hot reload applied (agents.list)` after changing `agents.<id>.model.primary`, but the in-memory model resolver returns the pre-change value. The stale session runtime metadata (`modelProvider`/`model`) is treated as authoritative over current config defaults. This is a false-success signal — the log implies the change was applied while it was silently ignored. Fixing this eliminates the need for a full gateway restart to pick up a model config change.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: `resolveSessionModelRef` returns stale `modelProvider`/`model` instead of re-resolving from current agent defaults after a hot-reload.
- Real environment tested: Linux (Node 24), `fix/session-model-hot-reload-102269` branch.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts --run
  ```

- Evidence after fix:

  ```console
   Test Files  4 passed (4)
        Tests  484 passed (484)
     Start at  06:59:26
     Duration  78.50s
  
  New test cases (3):
  • "returns runtime metadata when it still matches current agent defaults"
    — agent config = anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6, entry runtime = anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
    → returns { anthropic, claude-sonnet-4-6 } (cache valid, no overhead)
  
  • "re-resolves from current config when runtime metadata is stale after hot-reload"
    — agent config = anthropic/claude-opus-4-6, entry runtime = anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 (stale)
    → returns { anthropic, claude-opus-4-6 } (re-resolved from config)
  
  • "preserves runtime metadata when agentId is not provided (backward compat)"
    — no agentId, runtime = openai/gpt-5.4, config = anthropic/claude-opus-4-6
    → returns { openai, gpt-5.4 } (unchanged behavior)
  ```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. When session runtime metadata matches current agent defaults → returns cached values immediately (zero overhead in steady state)
  2. When session runtime metadata differs from current defaults → re-resolves from config (picks up hot-reloaded model)
  3. Callers without `agentId` → unchanged behavior (conservative backward compat)
- What was not tested: Full E2E gateway restart-and-repro scenario (the fix is proven at the pure-function level by unit tests; a live E2E test requires provider credentials and file-watcher setup)

## Root Cause (if applicable)

After a session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset` in `session-reset-service.ts:1127-1128`), the resolved model is stored as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. On subsequent calls, `resolveSessionModelRef` (`session-utils.ts:1647-1648`) returns these cached values directly without checking whether the agent config has changed since the reset. When `agents.list` is hot-reloaded, the reload handler (`server-reload-handlers.ts:367`) resets the model catalog but does not invalidate per-session runtime model metadata. New child sessions inherit the stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection` (`session-create-service.ts:124-125`).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

After changing `agents.<id>.model.primary` and triggering a config hot-reload, new turns and fresh threads (created via `/new`) now pick up the new model immediately instead of remaining on the stale pre-reload model.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Config changed vs unchanged, agentId provided vs absent, runtime metadata matching vs stale
- Edge cases checked: Explicit overrides (`modelOverride`/`providerOverride`) still take precedence; no-agentId fallback unchanged; session with only one of `modelProvider`/`model` present (fallthrough path unchanged)
- What you did NOT verify: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); channel integration tests

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds a staleness check before the existing early return; all existing code paths and behaviors preserved
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Adding the staleness check in the shared `resolveSessionModelRef` is the correct boundary because it catches the issue for all callers (chat turns, tool execution, status display, session creation) without requiring changes to the hot-reload handler, session persistence layer, or `/new` inheritance logic.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Invalidating session entries in the hot-reload handler (`server-reload-handlers.ts`). Rejected because it requires iterating and mutating all session store files, which is more complex and error-prone than the single-function approach.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: False positive — could a session intentionally have `modelProvider`/`model` different from agent defaults? No: these fields are only set during session reset from `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` output. User explicit selections use `modelOverride`/`providerOverride` which are handled in a separate code path.
- **Mitigation**: The staleness check uses `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` which is the same function that originally produced the cached values, ensuring identical semantics.
- **Compatibility**: No breaking changes. Callers without `agentId` preserve existing behavior.

---

Related to #102269
